newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African arms end up with Sudan rebels - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: S.African arms end up with Sudan rebels - newspaper.

text.p: South African arms sold to Uganda have ended up in the hands of rebels in Sudan, the Johannesburg Sunday Independent said.

"Weapons, including armoured vehicles, that have been sold to Uganda have ended up in the hands of the Sudanese People's Liberation Army (SPLA), said sources in the Ugandan capital Kampala," the paper reported.
"A source in Kampala said reports from the southern Sudan warfront stated that anti-tank missiles and a mine-clearer of South African origin were in use by the rebel forces."
It said Uganda was supporting the SPLA, which is fighting the Islamic government of neighbouring Sudan.

The newspaper quoted South African government sources as saying arms sales to Uganda could upset President Nelson Mandela's efforts to broker a peace in Zaire, which accuses Uganda of backing rebels in its country.
Officials in Pretoria confirmed to the Sunday Independent that the cabinet approved arms sales of an undisclosed value to Uganda last year, but said it had no dealings with the SPLA.

Pretoria, which has pledged not to sell arms to conflict zones, cancelled a planned arms sale to Rwanda late last year after fighting flared across its border in eastern Zaire, where rebels are making advances against the army.
It has also rowed back from a planned sale of arms to Syria that angered the United States. South Africa now says it will consult with Washington over the deal.
